questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I really wanted to experience the culture of australia, as it is a place that i have always thought was filled with interesting and nice people, which i really think it is. I have been able to get to know loads of new people and gotten a better understanding of their different circumstances and cultural backgrounds.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was not a problem whatsoever

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Not much, it wasnt really a necessity

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer:
UTS has on-campus housing which has been very nice, as it has been very easy to meet a lot of new people (i think 600 people live here across 13 floors)

i have lived in a 6-share apartment but there were also other options such as single rooms, two shares or woman only 6-shares

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: there are great cooking facilities in every 6-share apartment

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: I think its a great place to live if you want a social life filled with spontaneity as well as an easy way to meet lots of new people.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I have heard that a lot of people got rejected which is unfortunate.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: There were a few things you had to show up to in the first week in order to get information on your classes and other school activities. You just registered online.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The school has pretty good communication and you can message all your teachers. There were also U-pass lessons which were supposed to easy the access to older students that had already passed whatever subject you have, but i didnt go to a U-pass lesson

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got the ones i wanted

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Read up on what subjects you want and consider contacting someone local to make sure you get the correct subjects you want. Some subjects are super easy and are a free pass, some of them are super interesting where as others not as much. Your subjects can define how you end up spending your time - as an example I have heard that the architecture program is extremely stressfull because of the workload and wouldnt recommend it.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I think "Introduction to engineering projects" was a terrible subject but every other one i had was good

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level of courses were pretty good except for one that was obviously for first years

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: I think it was pretty similar. except for Introduction to Engineering projects it was really weird and focused on talking a lot in class

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Programming 1
Strategic design making and game theory
Introduction to Engineering projects
The Social Life of Technology

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Programming 1 was good for learning java and python and i generally liked the structure of it

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Lots of them, you could join almost any genre of community. I Joined a climbing and a calisthenics club that were both great

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Skydiving. Travelling :)

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: go on roadtrips to red cliff campground its insane. go to the beaches. go to byron bay. just spend a lot of time with your friends :D

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: I had no problems

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: I think you just have to start a conversation even though it can be awkward. If you just see someone enough times and talk to them, it will eventually feel natural even if awkward at first. It can be somewhat hard to find locals as most of the people you meet naturally are also on exchange, but it is all about putting yourself out there and being open to experiences.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Language took a little bit of getting used to as there are a lot of shortening of words or other slang, but it wasnt a big deal

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: how open everyone is and how a lot of people are chill

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Travel a lot with good friends
Put yourself out there and dont be afraid to have awkward conversations. 
Take a lot of pictures

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Nah youll be alright just have fun

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: All of the friendships i made

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: I got sick 6 times throughout my stay, i think because i live in a building with people from immune systems that are from all over the world - possibly leading to diseases my body is not used to.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
